text:
Aisha (Support): Hey team — customer Beth is seeing streaming responses fail mid-stream. They report client-side errors and our dashboards showed a sharp spike in 5xx for the gateway around 15:12 PST. Repro steps attached from the customer below.

Beth (Customer): FYI this happens with our node client using chunked transfer. We start getting partial output then connection drops; from our side it’s a socket error: \"write ECONNRESET\". Happens ~1/200 requests.

Sam (Support): Added logs from the customer: their client sends a chunked POST and then closes the socket after ~3s. They say they didn't cancel intentionally; their client threw due to internal timeout.

Beth (Customer): Here's the minimal curl that mimics it for us:
```
curl -i -N -X POST \\"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream" \\\-H \\"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\-H \\"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \\\\--data-binary $'{"input":"start","stream":true}' \\--max-time 3
```
If curl's max-time triggers it, we see our client get ECONNRESET and on your metrics this increments 5xx in the gateway.

Marco (SRE): Thanks, reproducer is helpful. I correlated the spike to 15:12:03-15:14:10 and saw many upstream errors logged as \"connection reset by peer\" in the gateway. Example from gateway.log: 
```
[2026-03-10T15:12:45Z] upstream: 10.4.12.8:8080, id=abc123, status=502, msg=\"recv(): Connection reset by peer\"
```
But the observability pipeline converted these to 5xx (502/504) counts for customer-facing metrics.

Jin (Eng-Infra): Is the upstream actually returning 502, or is the gateway failing to get a response because the client closed the connection? Those are different. If client closed the socket while we were streaming, NGINX usually returns 499 (client closed request). Our metric ingestion might treat 499 as 5xx by mistake.

Eve (Eng-Infra): I dug into ingestion code. We have a translation table that maps raw gateway status -> metric buckets. There's a bug: statuses >= 400 are grouped, but 499 gets folded into the 5xx cohort because we coerce nonstandard codes to 500-range when there's a missing field. Looks like a null status is mapping to 500.

Marco (SRE): Confirmed: many logs show \"client prematurely closed connection\" followed by no upstream status. The parser then emits status = null which the aggregator treats as 500. That explains why customer-side cancels are counted as 5xx.

Aisha (Support): Customer is worried because they see downtime-credit triggers. Can we distinguish true upstream 5xx vs client-abort?

Jin (Eng-Infra): Short-term: add a metric for \"gateway.client_abort\" when we detect EOF/client reset before upstream responds. That will let us separate counts in dashboards. Medium-term: fix the mapper to preserve 499 (or emit a distinct classification) instead of coercing to 500.

Marco (SRE): I'll add an alert suppression rule so SLA-calculator ignores spikes where client_abort ratio > 50% for that minute. Don't want to auto-credit for user-side timeouts.

Eve (Eng-Infra): Patch ready:
```
# in metrics_mapper.py
-if status is None:
-    status_bucket = 500
+if status is None and reason == \"client_close\":
+    status_bucket = 499
+elif status is None:
+    status_bucket = 500
```
I'll open PR and request review. Need canary to verify we still classify true upstream errors as 5xx.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout queued for metrics-mapper v2026.03.10. Next window at 16:00 UTC.

Sam (Support): Repro notes for Eng: customer provided these exact steps:
1) Start a streaming request (chunked) that yields tokens slowly (~250ms per chunk).
2) After first chunk, client triggers a local timeout and closes socket.
3) Customer sees client ECONNRESET, our gateway logs show \"upstream hangup\" and metrics spike as 5xx.

Marco (SRE): Can reproduce locally with the curl max-time snippet. I ran a load test to simulate 1000 streams with 0.5% random client aborts; current metrics show a 10% 5xx spike because of the mapping bug. After applying Eve's local patch, the 5xx rate remains stable and we surface client_abort events.

Jin (Eng-Infra): For the longer fix, we should also update our API SDKs' default socket timeouts + best-practice guidance. Many clients treat stream timeouts as hard aborts. We can add retries on idempotent streaming calls or recommend client keepalive.

Beth (Customer): Appreciate the quick triage. If you can suppress the SLA hit for our org while you fix, that would help — our billing team is watching the spike.

Aisha (Support): Filing an internal billing exception w/ finance, tagging this thread. Finance note: please hold auto-credit until SRE confirms classification.

Marco (SRE): Actions assigned:
- Eve: PR and canary metrics-mapper (in review) — target 16:00 UTC.
- Marco: Add temporary SLA suppression rule — target 15:50 UTC.
- Jin: Prepare SDK guidance blurb and add to support KB — target EOD.
- Sam/Aisha: Keep Beth updated.

incident-bot: Incident created INC-20260310-47: \"Streaming client aborts misclassified as 5xx\". Priority: P3.

Eve (Eng-Infra): PR merged to canary branch. Canary shows reduced 5xx and a new metric \"gateway.client_abort.count\". Sample canary log: 
```
[2026-03-10T16:02:12Z] event=client_abort id=def456 reason=EOF
[2026-03-10T16:02:12Z] metric.gateway.client_abort.count=1
```

Marco (SRE): Suppression rule in place. SLA calculator will ignore minutes where client_abort > 40% of total errors for a tenant.

Aisha (Support): Beth — we've deployed a fix to classify client aborts separately and suppressed SLA hits for the window where this occurred. Please confirm if you still see ECONNRESET spikes after 16:05 UTC.

Beth (Customer): Confirmed — traffic looks normal now, no more big 5xx bump. Thank you! :tada:

Sam (Support): Closing the customer-facing ticket; will keep incident open until we roll the backend fix to stable and update docs.

Jin (Eng-Infra): Follow-ups:
- Roll canary to stable after 24h of no regressions.
- Add unit tests in metrics-mapper for null_status + reason mapping.
- Update public KB: \"Why streaming requests show 5xx\" with recommended client timeout defaults.

Eve (Eng-Infra): I'll create the PR for stable rollout and add the tests.

Aisha (Support): Thanks everyone. Good cross-team response. :heart:
